stories.body: The death toll from catastrophic floods along the Nepal-Tibet border has passed 1,000, while more than 3,900 people remain missing, including hundreds of hydropower workers feared trapped in mud-filled tunnels. Rescue teams from Nepal and China, supported by specialists from India, South Korea and Australia, are contending with unstable terrain, high water and widespread destruction of bridges and infrastructure. Authorities say hundreds have been rescued, but relatives of missing workers fear diminishing oxygen supplies as engineers try to locate and clear the tunnels.
stories.headline: Nepal and Tibet flood death toll passes 1,000 as rescuers search hydropower tunnels

stories.body: The United States and Iran exchanged fire for the first time in a month after Washington said it struck Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the Strait of Hormuz to prevent the deployment of new mines. Iran responded by saying it fired ballistic missiles at US-operated bases in Jordan, while the United Arab Emirates said it intercepted a drone over its waters. President Donald Trump threatened a further response as the conflict continues to disrupt shipping through the strategically vital strait, though Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran remained open to implementing a US agreement mediated by Pakistan.
stories.headline: US and Iran exchange fire again as Trump threatens further action

stories.body: At least 12 people were killed and more than 20 injured in overnight Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region, Ukrainian officials said. Six of those killed were railway workers after a depot in the capital was hit, while four others died when a residential building in Boryspil was struck. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attacks underscored Ukraine's shortage of air-defence systems, as Russia said it had targeted military and energy facilities and Ukraine reported drone strikes on Russian oil and port infrastructure.
stories.headline: Russian drone and missile barrage kills at least 12 in Kyiv

stories.body: Fast-fashion retailer Shein's shares fell as much as 10% in their Hong Kong market debut before closing around 4% below the offer price, after the company raised HK$13.6 billion in its long-delayed initial public offering. The Singapore-headquartered, China-founded company was valued at about $26 billion, far below its nearly $100 billion valuation in 2022. Its listing follows failed plans in New York and London amid scrutiny over labour practices, environmental concerns and its supply chain, while new import duties and intensifying competition have put pressure on its low-cost business model.
stories.headline: Shein shares fall in Hong Kong market debut

stories.body: The European Union is considering a three-year military and civilian mission to advise and train Lebanon's army and internal security forces as the UN peacekeeping mandate in southern Lebanon is due to expire at the end of 2026. The proposal would focus on border and maritime security rather than fully replace UNIFIL, whose nearly 50-year mission has monitored the area without authority to enforce an Israeli withdrawal or disarm armed groups. Analysts warn that the end of UNIFIL could create a dangerous security vacuum while Israeli strikes and occupation continue in southern Lebanon.
stories.headline: EU considers mission to replace departing UN peacekeepers in southern Lebanon

stories.body: Vice President JD Vance sought to reassure the Republican Jewish Coalition in a closed-door speech in Las Vegas, addressing concerns over rising antisemitism, his relationship with Israel-sceptical media figures and declining support for Israel among younger Americans. Vance argued that Republicans should explain the US-Israel relationship in terms of concrete national interests, condemned antisemitic theories and said hatred of Jews was corrosive. The appearance was seen as an effort to strengthen his standing with pro-Israel Republican donors and activists ahead of a possible 2028 presidential bid.
stories.headline: Vance courts pro-Israel Republicans while addressing antisemitism and support for Israel

stories.body: Flash flooding in the Grand Canyon has killed at least two people and left others missing or unaccounted for as search and rescue operations continue. About 50 hikers were airlifted from the area, trails were closed and the flooding damaged a footbridge and the sole water pipeline serving tourists and residents. Officials have cautioned that establishing an accurate count of those still missing has been difficult.
stories.headline: Grand Canyon flash flood leaves two dead as search and rescue efforts continue

stories.body: The Federal Trade Commission and attorneys general from 22 states have sued Amazon, alleging that it secretly manipulated advertising auctions to overcharge more than one million advertisers by an estimated $20 billion since 2019. The complaint says Amazon often replaced expected second-price auction results with higher charges close to winning bidders' own bids, with costs potentially passed on to shoppers. Amazon strongly disputed the allegations, saying the FTC misunderstands its advertising system and that advertisers adjust bids based on performance.
stories.headline: FTC and 22 states sue Amazon, alleging it inflated advertising prices

stories.body: Tropical Storm Edouard is expected to strengthen before making landfall on the Texas coast, bringing heavy rain and a serious risk of flash flooding to parts of Texas and Louisiana. Early Tuesday, the storm had sustained winds of 40 mph and was moving west-northwest near the Gulf Coast. Forecasters expect 3 to 6 inches of rain around Houston, with isolated totals of up to 9 inches, while authorities warned that intense hourly rainfall could rapidly flood low-lying and urban areas.
stories.headline: Tropical Storm Edouard threatens Texas and Louisiana as another storm approaches Hawaii

stories.body: California lawmakers are expected to vote on a narrower wildfire-reform bill after rejecting key elements of Governor Gavin Newsom's proposal to limit utilities' financial liability for fires caused by their equipment. The compromise is intended to help survivors receive payments more quickly, but Newsom said it falls short of the broad changes needed to resolve who should bear the costs of utility-caused wildfires. His original plan would have reduced payments for some victims and prevented insurers from seeking reimbursement from electrical companies.
stories.headline: California lawmakers prepare to vote on wildfire reforms after rejecting key parts of Newsom's plan

stories.body: Spain's government is set to approve a €168 million emergency support package for Ceuta as the city continues to grapple with a month-long migration crisis. The plan includes direct aid for businesses and self-employed workers, support for tourism and public services, expanded employment protections and subsidies for employers, alongside separate funding for water supplies and migrant children. Tens of thousands of people are reported to have crossed the border during the crisis, leaving thousands in Ceuta and prompting continued protests, strained local services and political criticism of the government's response.
stories.headline: Spain's Ceuta migration crisis deepens as the government prepares a €168 million emergency package

stories.body: Annual inflation in the eurozone rose to 3.3% in August, up four-tenths of a percentage point from July and its highest reading in more than three years, according to Eurostat. Energy prices, which rose 14.3%, were the principal driver amid the effects of conflict in the Middle East. Spain recorded inflation of 4.5%, among the highest rates in the eurozone, and the data increases pressure on the European Central Bank to consider raising interest rates at its meeting on 10 September.
stories.headline: Eurozone inflation rises to 3.3%, its highest level in three years

stories.body: International visitors spent a record €18.218 billion in Spain in July, 10.9% more than a year earlier, according to provisional data from the National Statistics Institute. Average spending reached €1,579 per tourist, with the United Kingdom remaining the largest source market by expenditure, followed by Germany and France. The figures extend a record year for foreign tourism, with the Balearic Islands receiving the largest share of July spending, ahead of Catalonia and Andalusia.
stories.headline: Foreign tourist spending in Spain reaches a new July record

stories.body: Catalonia's education department has opened disciplinary proceedings against three employees after errors in the selection of students left the region's results excluded from comparative PISA rankings. The exclusion rate reached 23.2%, far above the OECD's recommended 5% limit, and the department said warnings from Spain's education ministry during the testing period were not passed on to schools or senior officials. Education minister Esther Niubó said the investigation found failures of interpretation, supervision and communication, while the department also announced the dismissal of its secretary-general.
stories.headline: Catalonia launches an investigation after an error leaves it out of the PISA assessment

stories.body: Barcelona recorded its hottest summer since observations began at the Fabra Observatory in 1914, with an average temperature of 27.1C from June through August, 0.4C above the previous record set in 2003. August was the second-warmest August in the observatory's record, averaging 27.9C, while rainfall was only 27% of its normal level. The summer also included a new absolute temperature record of 40.9C on 8 July and an unprecedented 31 July days with highs of at least 30C.
stories.headline: Barcelona records its hottest summer on record, with August among the warmest in more than a century

stories.body: Five years after tolls were removed from the AP-7 and other Catalan motorways, overall road deaths have declined but the AP-7 has seen more breakdowns, serious injuries and incidents involving trucks. Traffic on some stretches now reaches 150,000 vehicles a day, including 25,000 heavy vehicles, and breakdowns on the AP-7 rose 40% in the first seven months of 2026 compared with a year earlier. Catalonia's traffic authority says the central stretch between El Papiol and Mollet del Vallès is especially problematic and will consider variable tolling as one possible way to shift traffic away from peak periods.
stories.headline: Five years after tolls were removed, AP-7 breakdowns and truck-related incidents are rising

stories.body: Unions representing Barcelona library workers have called for a strike intended to close all 41 city libraries as a dispute over hours, pay and working conditions enters its fourth month. Workers say rotating schedules, long split shifts and weekend work leave them working substantially more days than staff on a standard five-day week, and they are demanding a supplement for public-facing duties. The city council says it remains open to negotiations and has backed an agreement with other unions that includes an 8% pay increase and a 35-hour week, while reporting that most libraries have remained open during the action.
stories.headline: Barcelona libraries call for a citywide closure as their protest escalates
